_comment: Fleet provider registry. Copy to ./.fleet/providers.json (project) or ~/.fleet/providers.json (user) and edit to match what YOU actually have access to. Run /fleet-init to have Claude draft this for you with current models and pricing. Fields: enabled, adapter (codex|gemini|opencode), access (subscription|api|local|free), default_model (REQUIRED for opencode, provider/model form; empty elsewhere = CLI default), max_workers, cost, strengths/weaknesses (short, honest, yours — these steer routing), context_window, trust (standard|restricted), notes. Optional per-provider: soft_weekly_cap {tasks and/or tokens} for quota pacing, review_after (ISO date) for scheduled access-term changes.

cost.notes: ChatGPT plan — flat-rate marginal cost until usage limits hit

weaknesses: subscription quota is opaque — limits appear without warning
codex.notes: First-party OpenAI harness. Resume supported. soft_weekly_cap is a self-imposed pacing proxy for the plan's invisible usage limits — tune it to your plan; the fleet deprioritizes (not blocks) this provider as delegated usage approaches it.

cost.notes: Free tier with Google login: ~60 req/min, ~1000/day. API key mode is per-token.

strengths: generous free tier for bulk mechanical work
weaknesses: no headless session resume — follow-ups need fresh briefs
quality drops when free tier silently falls back to flash
gemini.notes: First-party Google harness. Headless returns one JSON object at the end, so no live progress events.

cost.notes: VERIFY current pricing before enabling — this is an example placeholder

weaknesses: weaker multi-step agentic reliability than frontier harnesses
deepseek.notes: Runs through OpenCode. Requires: opencode auth login (deepseek API key).

cost.notes: Local inference — free but occupies the machine

strengths: private — code never leaves the machine
weaknesses: local models fail verification more on multi-step agentic work
local-lmstudio.notes: LM Studio via its OpenAI-compatible endpoint, configured as a provider in opencode.json. Set default_model to the exact provider/model name from `opencode models`. restricted trust: only dispatch small, low-blast-radius tasks.

cost.notes: Claude plan — flat-rate. API-key auth is per_token; claude reports total_cost_usd per run either way.

weaknesses: if the supervisor is Claude Code on the same account, this spends the same quota — parallelism only, not a cost play
claude-worker.notes: Claude Code headless (claude -p). Main uses: non-Claude supervisors (e.g. Codex running fleet) dispatching Claude workers, or a Claude supervisor dispatching haiku for cheap tasks. Resume supported (directory-scoped). review_after: set this to any date a provider's access terms are scheduled to change (e.g. a frontier model moving from subscription tiers to usage credits) — registry.py list flags REVIEW_DUE once it passes, reminding you to re-verify access/cost and update caps.

routing._comment: Cheapest-first cascade the supervisor consults AFTER capability filtering. Order reflects cost: local free -> subscription/free flat -> API per-token. Reorder to taste; the ledger's track record can override this for specific task types.
